source.title: The Spotlight Resonance Method: Resolving the Alignment of Embedded Activations

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different measurement method (Spotlight-Resonance) to examine alignment with neuron-like privileged directions and reports preliminary local-coding results. It does not measure the claim versions’ stated explanation shares or evaluate explanation predictions on held-out activations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports alignment measurements and preliminary analyses of selected dataset subsets. It explicitly cautions that global alignment does not establish local coding across a whole network. No proportions of poles with one job, two jobs, or unexplained jobs are reported; no explanation-prediction test on activations is reported. Cited results from other work and threshold values used to configure the method are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It uses Spotlight-Resonance to measure whether latent activations in small MNIST/CIFAR autoencoders cluster around directions privileged by the activation function. It reports no share of neurons with one main job, no language models, no InceptionV1 analysis, no attribution graphs, and no explanation scoring. Its finding that the activation function causes basis alignment is close to V4's architecture argument. It does not measure an interpretable-neuron share or compare tools, so it is a related construct (fits_no_version), not a test. The record's 'tests/T2' is corrected.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also claims a direct causal link: activation-function symmetry breaking causes representational alignment, so the standard neuron basis is not inherently special. Grandmother-neuron examples are preliminary, and the author notes they are not universal (some neurons showed no class variation).
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces Spotlight-Resonance, a rotation-and-counting measure of activation alignment with privileged basis directions. It does not use the original neuron-explanation auditing or held-out explanation-scoring recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported signal varies with privileged basis, basis completeness, model size, and spotlight threshold epsilon. Some networks required lower epsilon; simplex-basis models included both anti-alignment and alignment depending on model variety.

fits_no_version.finding: In small tanh-variant autoencoders trained with isotropic choices, latent activations align or anti-align with the basis privileged by the activation function. They do not align with the standard or a random basis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-function functional form, not the neuron basis itself, causes representations to cluster along privileged directions. This is related to V4's architecture argument but measures alignment, not interpretability share.

record.peer_reviewed: To appear at the ICLR 2025 Workshop on Representational Alignment (Re-Align)
record.problems: The author describes the local-coding analyses as preliminary, uses hand-picked directions and subjective interpretations, and says they do not establish local coding across the full network. The study tests small autoencoders rather than language models and does not report uncertainty estimates or quantitative shares of interpretable units. Several alignment outcomes are presented only in figures, with qualitative descriptions in the text.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or shares of single-job, two-job or unexplained neuron poles.
No language models, MoE models or scale comparison.
No InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, pose or recursive-generalization analysis.
No interpretable-neuron share and no tool comparison. Only shows the activation function induces basis alignment in small autoencoders.
No attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No test of activating-example explanations against firing prediction.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Workshop paper on small fully connected autoencoders. Alignment results are figure-only, with no uncertainty reported. Results depend on epsilon and basis type; simplex bases gave anti-alignment in small models. The second fits_no_version entry above is a placeholder artifact and should be ignored. The substantive second finding is the hand-picked grandmother-like directions (r6–r10), whose prevalence and explanation fidelity are not established.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or report the shares of poles with one job, two related jobs, or jobs not yet understood.
Does not test language models, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, or scaling to large parameter counts; it reports no comparable job shares.
Does not analyze the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose, or recursive generalization.

Does not estimate interpretable-neuron shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models or compare explanation tools. It studies effects of activation-function-induced privileged bases in small autoencoders.
Does not build attribution graphs or compare neuron-based explanations with a trained replacement model or reconstruction error.
Does not test explanations against where a neuron fires on new text or otherwise compare activating-example fit with firing prediction.
Does not score automated neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relation.reason: It discusses whether neurons correspond to human-interpretable concepts (local coding, grandmother neurons) only as context for its own alignment method.

tranche.reason: The study introduces SRM and measures whether latent activations in small MNIST/CIFAR autoencoders align with privileged bases set by the activation function. It reports no share of interpretable neurons, no LLMs and no InceptionV1 analysis, so it tests no version.

source_check.notes: All values are figure-only. Beyond the roughly 90% plane amplitude there are no numeric SRM values. The standard-vs-random-vs-privileged comparison (Fig. 2) is on one network; the text says other networks were consistent. Grandmother-neuron results (App. B.2, Figs 3-4) are preliminary, and the author says they are not universal. Fig. 9 (r15) is anti-aligned, like r13.
